title: Security
hired_for: An owner hires this screen so the store does not lose money to fraud, chargebacks and fake traffic, nobody takes over an account, and the business can recover within a day if something breaks.

jobs.job: Stop anyone taking over my store, ad, email or bank accounts
jobs.why: One stolen login can empty an ad account, change payout details or send a fake email to every customer. Two-step login on every admin account stops most of it.

watch.metric: share of admin and staff accounts with two-step login or a passkey across Shopify, Meta, Google, Klaviyo, the bank and the domain registrar, weekly
watch.source: Shopify staff accounts, Meta Business Manager, Google Admin, Klaviyo users

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 7 of 19 admin accounts have no two-step login, including 2 agency users on Meta. After: all 19 have it on within 1 week.

jobs.job: Be able to restore the store within a day
jobs.why: A bad app, a wrong bulk edit or a hack can wipe products, customers or the theme. A backup only counts if a restore has been tested.

watch.metric: days since the last successful restore test of products, customers, orders and theme
watch.source: backup app log (Rewind or similar), brand brain runbook

drives.metric: hours to recover from a data loss

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: backups run but no restore has ever been tried. After: a test restore of the theme and 100 products works and is repeated every 30 days.

jobs.job: Stop fraud orders before they ship
jobs.why: A fraud order loses the product, the postage and the sale, then adds a chargeback fee. Catching it before it ships saves all of it.

watch.metric: fraud loss: orders shipped then charged back as fraud, dollars per month
watch.source: Shopify fraud analysis and Shopify Payments disputes

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: $4,200 a month ships to fraud orders flagged high risk. After: high risk orders are held for review and fraud loss falls to $900 within 30 days.

jobs.job: Keep chargebacks under the payment processor's warning line
jobs.why: Past a set rate of disputes (often near 1% of orders), the processor adds fees, holds payouts or closes the account. Losing card payments stops the business.

watch.metric: disputes divided by orders, monthly, against the processor's warning line
watch.source: Shopify Payments or Stripe disputes, PayPal disputes

drives.metric: risk of held payouts or a closed payment account

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: disputes are 0.7% and rising. After: clearer billing names and faster refunds bring them to 0.3% within 2 months.

jobs.job: Keep domain and DNS locked down
jobs.why: If someone takes the domain, the store, email and ads all go dark. A registrar lock and a clean DNS list take an afternoon.

watch.metric: registrar lock and two-step login on the registrar, and count of DNS records pointing at nothing, weekly
watch.source: domain registrar, DNS provider

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the registrar has no lock and 3 old records point at closed services. After: the lock is on and all 3 are removed today.

jobs.job: Stop blocking good customers by mistake
jobs.why: Strict fraud rules and card checks turn away real buyers. A lost good order costs more than most fraud.

watch.metric: share of orders cancelled or declined as fraud that were later shown to be good, and payment approval rate, monthly
watch.source: Shopify fraud analysis, Shopify Payments or Stripe approval data

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 2.4% of orders are cancelled as risky and half of those were good. After: rules are tuned and false cancels fall to 0.6% within 30 days.

jobs.job: Remove access people should not have
jobs.why: Ex-staff, old agencies and staff with full admin rights they do not need are the easiest way in for a thief.

watch.metric: count of active accounts held by ex-staff or ex-agencies, and share of accounts reviewed in the last 90 days
watch.source: Shopify staff accounts, Meta Business Manager, Google, Klaviyo

drives.metric: accounts with more access than their role needs

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 5 people who left still have access and 8 staff have full admin. After: the 5 are removed and 6 of 8 move to limited roles within a week.

jobs.job: Keep checkout free of card-stealing scripts
jobs.why: A script on the checkout or payment page can copy card details. Card rules now ask stores to list and approve every script on payment pages.

watch.metric: count of third-party scripts on checkout and payment pages that are not on the approved list, weekly
watch.source: Shopify checkout settings and customer events, site script scan

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 11 scripts load on the thank you and checkout pages and 4 have no known owner. After: the 4 are removed and the list is checked every week.

jobs.job: Block card testing attacks
jobs.why: Fraudsters test stolen cards with many small orders in minutes. Each attempt costs fees, and a burst can trip the processor's alarms.

watch.metric: count of card testing bursts (many failed payments in a short window), daily
watch.source: Shopify Payments or Stripe payment logs

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 2 bursts last month brought 1,400 failed payments. After: bot checks at checkout and rate limits stop the next burst within minutes.

jobs.job: Stop fake emails sent in my brand's name
jobs.why: Without email checks at the strictest setting (DMARC at reject), anyone can send mail that looks like it came from the brand. It also hurts email reach.

watch.metric: email check setting per sending domain (none, quarantine or reject) and share of mail passing, weekly
watch.source: DNS records, DMARC reports, Klaviyo sending domain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the policy is set to none, so fake mail goes through. After: it moves to reject in 3 steps over 6 weeks with no drop in real mail.

jobs.job: Stop discount codes leaking and being abused
jobs.why: A code meant for one partner ends up on coupon sites and gets used on full price orders by customers who would have paid anyway.

watch.metric: share of orders using a code outside its intended audience, weekly
watch.source: Shopify discount reports

drives.metric: discount rate on full price orders

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: an influencer code is used on 900 orders a month, 70% from coupon sites. After: codes are single use or capped and leaked use falls 80% within a week.

jobs.job: Close serious security findings fast
jobs.why: A known weak spot left open is an open door. Critical findings should close within days, not months.

watch.metric: count of open critical and high findings and days each has been open, weekly
watch.source: weekly security scan results

drives.metric: findings open past their fix window

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 3 critical findings have been open for 40 days. After: all 3 close within 7 days and new ones close within a week.

jobs.job: Protect customer accounts from takeover
jobs.why: Stolen passwords from other sites get tried on the store. A taken account can drain store credit or send orders to a new address.

watch.metric: failed customer logins per hour against baseline, and accounts whose email or address changed right after a new-device login, daily
watch.source: Shopify customer accounts, bot protection logs

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a spike of 20,000 failed logins went unseen. After: login rate limits are on and spikes are flagged within the hour.

jobs.job: Keep bot traffic out of my numbers and my checkout
jobs.why: Bots inflate visits, drag down conversion rate, pollute ad audiences and hammer checkout. The owner needs to know how much traffic is not human.

watch.metric: share of sessions scored as bots, with the checkout share shown apart, daily against the brand's own baseline
watch.source: Cloudflare or platform bot reports, GA4

drives.metric: accuracy of conversion rate and ad audiences

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 22% of sessions are bots and nobody knows. After: bad bots are challenged and the bot share falls to 8%, lifting reported conversion to its true level.

jobs.job: Stop scammers pretending to be us
jobs.why: Lookalike sites and fake social ads use the brand's name and photos to steal payments. Customers blame the brand.

watch.metric: count of new lookalike domains and fake ads or pages using the brand, weekly
watch.source: domain watch service, Meta Ad Library search, customer reports in Gorgias

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 2 lookalike stores run Meta ads with the brand's photos. After: both are reported and taken down within 10 days and new ones are caught weekly.

jobs.job: Check every app, script and vendor that can touch customer data
jobs.why: Each app with access to customers or orders is another way in. Old apps nobody uses still hold that access.

watch.metric: count of installed apps and vendors with customer or order access that have not been reviewed in 90 days
watch.source: Shopify installed apps and their permissions, vendor list in the brand brain

drives.metric: apps with more access than they need

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 34 apps are installed, 9 unused, and 5 can read all customer data. After: the 9 are removed and access is cut on 3 more within 2 weeks.

jobs.job: Know what to do in the first hour of an incident
jobs.why: When a hack, a leak or a ransom note lands, a written plan with names and first steps saves hours and money.

watch.metric: written incident plan in place and days since the last practice run
watch.source: runbook in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: no written plan exists. After: a 1 page plan names who does what and a 30 minute practice runs every 6 months.

jobs.job: Win the disputes I should win
jobs.why: Many disputes are customers who forgot a purchase or claim it never came. With order, delivery and contact records, most can be won.

watch.metric: dispute win rate and dollars recovered, monthly
watch.source: Shopify Payments or Stripe disputes, carrier tracking

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the brand answers 30% of disputes and wins 20% of those. After: every dispute gets a proof pack and the win rate reaches 55% within 60 days.

jobs.job: Stay on the right side of privacy laws
jobs.why: US state privacy laws and EU rules set how data is collected and when customers can ask for it back. A missed request or a tag firing before consent can bring fines.

watch.metric: share of tags firing only after consent where required, and customer data requests open past the legal deadline
watch.source: consent banner logs, Shopify customer privacy requests

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 4 tags fire before consent and 2 data requests are 50 days old. After: the tags wait for consent and both requests close this week.

jobs.job: Train staff to spot phishing
jobs.why: Most breaches start with a staff member clicking a fake login email. Short, regular practice cuts the click rate.

watch.metric: share of staff who clicked the last practice phishing email, quarterly
watch.source: phishing practice tool

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: no training runs. After: the first practice email gets 30% clicks, and the third one 6 months later gets 8%.

jobs.job: Rotate keys and passwords for connected tools on time
jobs.why: Old API keys shared with past agencies or apps stay valid for years. A leaked key can read orders or customers.

watch.metric: count of API keys and access tokens overdue for rotation or unused for 90 days, monthly
watch.source: key list in the brand brain, Shopify custom apps, platform settings

drives.metric: keys held by people or apps no longer in use

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 12 keys exist and 5 belong to past agencies. After: the 5 are revoked and the rest rotate every 90 days.

jobs.job: Stop resale bots from buying up limited drops
jobs.why: When a limited product sells out in minutes to bots, real fans leave angry and the items show up on resale sites.

watch.metric: share of drop units bought by accounts that share a card, address or device, per drop
watch.source: Shopify orders, bot protection logs

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 25% of the last drop went to 30 linked accounts. After: order limits and bot checks cut that to under 5% on the next drop.

jobs.job: Stop return and refund abuse
jobs.why: A small group of customers returns most of what they buy or claims items never came. Left alone, the cost grows.

watch.metric: share of refund dollars going to customers who returned most of their last orders, monthly
watch.source: Shopify returns and refunds, Gorgias

drives.metric: refund cost as a share of sales

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 40 customers took $6,000 in refunds last quarter, returning 8 of every 10 orders. After: they are flagged, returns need review, and that cost halves.

jobs.job: Confirm which card security rules apply to us once a year
jobs.why: Card rules (PCI) differ by how the checkout is built. Using a hosted checkout keeps the rules light, but a change can quietly widen them.

watch.metric: card security self-check type confirmed and the date it was last confirmed
watch.source: payment processor account and the brand brain

drives.metric: risk of fines or losing card payments

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: nobody knows which self-check applies. After: the processor confirms it in writing and the date is logged for next year.

jobs.job: Set rules for AI shopping agents and crawlers
jobs.why: AI assistants and shopping agents now visit and even buy. Blocking all of them loses sales; allowing all of them invites scraping and fraud.

watch.metric: AI agent and crawler visits by type and what they did (browse, cart, checkout), weekly
watch.source: Cloudflare or platform bot reports, GA4 AI referral sessions

drives.metric: orders from AI assistants and agents

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: all bots get the same treatment. After: known AI assistants can browse, unknown agents are challenged at checkout, and AI referral orders are tracked.
